question: Which of these is the main reproductive organ in females?
explanation: Spot on! The ovaries are the primary organs because they make the eggs and female hormones. The rest are helper structures. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of the accessory (helper) female reproductive organs?

options.A: To support fertilization, gestation, and childbirth
options.B: To produce female hormones and mature eggs
options.C: To filter toxins from the pelvic blood supply
options.D: To regulate the monthly menstrual bleeding cycle

explanation: You got it! While ovaries make the eggs, the accessory organs provide the pathways, protection, and home for a baby to grow. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h1)

question: Where does fertilization usually happen inside the fallopian tube?
explanation: Brilliant! The ampulla is the wide middle part of the tube where the sperm and egg love to meet. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h2)

question: How do the fallopian tubes move an egg toward the uterus?

options.A: Using tiny waving cilia and smooth muscle contractions
options.B: By producing strong chemical suction currents
options.C: Using pulsating pressure from nearby arterial blood flow
options.D: Through rapid gravity shifts in the pelvic cavity

explanation: Correct! Tiny hair-like cilia wave back and forth while the tube muscles gently push the egg along on its journey. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which layer of the uterus gives it the strong power to push out a baby during labor?
explanation: Well done! The myometrium is made of thick, strong muscle that contracts powerfully during childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h3)

question: What happens to the endometrium (lining of the uterus) when pregnancy does not happen?

options.A: It transforms into permanent scar tissue inside the cavity
options.B: It hardens into a protective barrier for the cervix
options.C: It travels up the fallopian tubes to dissolve in the ovary
options.D: It sheds and leaves the body as menstrual flow

explanation: Spot on! When there's no fertilized egg to welcome, hormone levels drop and this lining sheds during your period. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the normal environment of the vagina in a healthy woman of childbearing age?
explanation: You're right! Friendly bacteria called lactobacilli keep the vagina acidic to protect it from bad germs and infections. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why does the vaginal lining have folds called rugae?

options.A: To trap menstrual blood before it reaches the external opening
options.B: To allow the canal to stretch during childbirth and intercourse
options.C: To secrete large amounts of lubricating mucus during sexual arousal
options.D: To provide a secure anchor point for resident protective bacteria

explanation: Correct! Those folds give the vagina extra stretch so it can safely pass a baby and handle different sizes. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which glands release lubricating fluid near the vaginal opening during sexual arousal?
explanation: Spot on! The Bartholin glands (or greater vestibular glands) help provide natural lubrication. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of these structures sits right inside the vaginal vestibule?
explanation: Well done! The vestibule is the space where both the opening for urine (urethra) and the vagina are located. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the main artery that supplies blood to the uterus?
explanation: Easy and correct! The uterine arteries are the main highways delivering oxygenated blood to the womb. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know that lymph drainage differs between the upper and lower reproductive organs?

options.A: It determines the specific pathway by which infections and cancer cells spread
options.B: It prevents accidental rupture of major arteries during routine examinations
options.C: It dictates the exact rate of intravenous fluid absorption in pelvic tissues
options.D: It controls the hormonal feedback loops regulating monthly ovulation cycles

explanation: You got it! Knowing where lymph drains helps us track how infections travel and how diseases like cancer might spread in the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why can an untreated lower vaginal infection lead to problems with getting pregnant?

options.A: Infections can travel upward through the uterus and scar the fallopian tubes
options.B: Bacterial toxins permanently stop the pituitary gland from releasing hormones
options.C: Inflammation completely closes the outer vaginal opening with scar tissue
options.D: Microbes directly destroy all developing eggs stored inside the ovaries

explanation: Spot on! Infections can move up (like in pelvic inflammatory disease) and leave scars that block the tubes, making it hard for eggs to travel. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h7)

question: A patient comes in with lower belly pain and a history of pelvic infections. Which tube-related complication should a nurse watch for closely?
explanation: Brilliant! Scarred fallopian tubes can trap a fertilized egg, leading to an ectopic pregnancy outside the uterus. Always keep an eye out for this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h7)
